prompt:
Draw: An inventory icon of a red apple with a small green leaf.
Canvas: exactly 16x16 pixels per frame.
Palette: use only these 32 colors and transparent, no others: #BE4A2F #D77643 #EAD4AA #E4A672 #B86F50 #733E39 #3E2731 #A22633 #E43B44 #F77622 #FEAE34 #FEE761 #63C74D #3E8948 #265C42 #193C3E #124E89 #0099DB #2CE8F5 #FFFFFF #C0CBDC #8B9BB4 #5A6988 #3A4466 #262B44 #181425 #FF0044 #68386C #B55088 #F6757A #E8B796 #C28569.
Background: transparent.
Safe area: draw the icon about the size of the central 14x14 pixels - rows 2-15 and columns 2-15, counting rows and columns from 1 - inside a 1-pixel margin on every side. That is a target for its average size, not a wall: when a pose or a detail needs the room (a raised weapon, a long blade, an effect, a wide stance), it may reach past the safe area into the margin, up to the canvas edge. Keep the four corner pixels transparent.
Style: clean, readable pixel art for a 2D RPG: a dark (not pure black) outline around the silhouette, 2-3 shades per material, light from the top-left, no anti-aliasing noise and no stray single pixels.

Output format: exactly one fenced code block tagged `pixels`, and nothing after it:
```pixels
PALETTE
. transparent
a #RRGGBB
b #RRGGBB
...
FRAME <frame name>
<16 lines, each exactly 16 characters>
...
END
```
- Each palette line is one key character and one #RRGGBB color. Keys are single characters from a-z, A-Z, 0-9; `.` is always transparent and is never redefined.
- Each frame is exactly 16 lines of exactly 16 characters, every character a palette key, with no spaces.
- Frames in this order: icon. Write `FRAME <name>` before each frame and `END` once after the last frame.
